title: Prepare and preview a target file
explanation: Create a one-host input file, then inspect its expanded targets.
options: The printf line replaces targets.txt. -iL reads targets; -sL -n previews without target probes or reverse DNS.

title: Scan an approved target list
explanation: Read scan scope from the file prepared above.
options: Inspect the file before every run; edited lists can change scope.

title: Explicit ARP discovery
explanation: Discover devices on your directly attached host-only lab segment.
options: -PR uses ARP for IPv4 local-link discovery. It cannot discover through a router; match the subnet to your actual lab.

title: TCP-based host discovery
explanation: Use selected TCP SYN probes to test lab-host reachability.
options: A response indicates reachability, not that every listed port is open. Local Ethernet targets normally still use ARP discovery.
result: A host-up result or no response.

title: Compare firewall filtering with ACK probes
explanation: Inspect filtering behavior on an owned lab host.
options: ACK scans distinguish filtered from unfiltered, not open from closed. Compare with a normal TCP scan.

title: Trace one local SYN probe sequence
explanation: Print the packets involved in a narrowly scoped scan.
options: Use one port to keep output readable. Trace data can reveal network details when shared.

title: Probe a UDP service more deeply
explanation: Combine UDP scanning with application probes against your lab DNS service.
options: A reply can resolve open|filtered ambiguity. Silence remains inconclusive.
result: UDP state and any recognized service.

title: Choose service-probe intensity
explanation: Choose a middle service-identification intensity.
options: Valid values are 0 through 9. Higher settings can send more probes without guaranteeing identification.

title: Trace service identification
explanation: Inspect diagnostic details of application probing.
options: Start the local web lab first. This is more verbose than ordinary -sV output.

title: Limit OS fingerprint retries
explanation: Limit repeated OS identification attempts on your lab VM.
options: Fewer attempts can reduce confidence. Open and closed TCP ports help fingerprint quality.
result: An OS estimate or insufficient evidence.

title: Trace the path to a lab host
explanation: Request hop information alongside discovery.
options: A directly attached VM may be one hop away. Filtering can leave some hops unknown.

title: Inspect local HTTP headers with NSE
explanation: Request and display headers from the local training service.
options: The script normally uses HEAD. A Server header is reported data, not independently verified software identity.

title: Inspect lab HTTP methods
explanation: Inspect method support on the disposable web lab.
options: This can send OPTIONS and additional method probes. Do not add test-all or retest casually; those can issue unsafe requests.
result: Method information if the server exposes it.

title: Audit a lab TLS cipher configuration
explanation: Enumerate offered TLS versions and ciphers on your own HTTPS service.
options: Makes many connections and is categorized as intrusive. Requires a TLS lab service; the plain HTTP lab is insufficient.
result: Protocol and cipher findings for review.

title: Inspect a lab SSH host key
explanation: Retrieve public host-key fingerprints from an owned SSH service.
options: Compare with a trusted fingerprint from its administrator. This does not authenticate a user or retrieve private keys.

title: Inventory SMB protocol versions
explanation: Query protocol dialects offered by an owned SMB server.
options: Requires an SMB lab service. Finding SMBv1 warrants review but does not itself demonstrate an exploit.

title: Select two HTTP scripts and a time limit
explanation: Run two named scripts on the local lab service.
options: The timeout applies to script instances, not the entire scan. Timed-out checks can leave incomplete output.
result: Title and header findings when available.

title: Inspect a specific HTTP path
explanation: Inspect headers for a particular local resource.
options: Quote the argument expression. The file index.html is created by the guided web lab.

title: Space probes apart
explanation: Insert a minimum interval between probes to the lab host.
options: This takes longer. Delay is not a guarantee of low load for every other scan phase.
result: Port states from a paced scan.

title: Reduce retry effort deliberately
explanation: Bound retransmission effort in a small lab check.
options: Packet loss can then produce incomplete or misleading results. Compare with default retries before concluding a service disappeared.

title: Resume an interrupted saved scan
explanation: Continue an interrupted scan from its normal-format report.
options: Requires a genuinely interrupted compatible report, not a finished file or XML-only output. Original scan settings are recovered; do not add new scan options.

title: Save a timestamped XML snapshot
explanation: Record a focused scan with a timestamp in its filename.
options: Run in the Kali shell; command substitution expands date. Two runs in the same second can use the same name.

title: Compare two XML scan reports
explanation: Compare the two reports created in Guided Lab 05.
options: Ndiff is a companion utility. Exit 0 means no differences, 1 means differences and 2 indicates an error.
result: Changed host, port or service information.

title: Export a machine-readable scan difference
explanation: Save the scan comparison as XML.
options: Redirection replaces changes.xml. A difference can reflect measurement conditions rather than a real configuration change.
